prerun_toolchain_measurement.finding: the linked exe is NOT byte-reproducible on this toolchain: g++ 15.2.0 MinGW-w64 emits PE timestamp fields -- exactly 2 bytes differ between two same-flag rebuilds of the same TU (cmp -l offsets 137 and 217 octal); the compiled OBJECT FILE is byte-reproducible (0 differing bytes across rebuilds, sha256 a759557e... == a759557e...).
prerun_toolchain_measurement.design_consequence: cache ENVELOPE integrity verifies the published bytes themselves (digest in meta); REBUILD reproducibility (F-CROSS-RUN-WRITE solo verification) compares the deterministic .o projection recorded in meta as determinism_digest, never the linked exe bytes.

amendment_windows_sharing.measured_during_validation: Windows refuses os.replace(staging, entry) while a reader holds the entry open (WinError 5), and a reader can see a transient sharing violation while a swap is in flight -- POSIX rename has neither behavior. Surfaced as a near-fire of F-PARTIAL-PUBLISH in the publish/read race (a reader crashed on PermissionError before the hardening).
amendment_windows_sharing.protocol_consequence: get() retries the open bounded (6x) and records 'io-contention' as a refusal (a miss -- never partial bytes); publish() retries os.replace bounded (8x) and fails CLEANLY on exhaustion. A reader still only ever observes: old complete entry, new complete entry, or miss.

theory.statement: Concurrent jobs need ZERO source-tree clones: one shared object store (the canonical sparse clone) serves N simultaneous jobs as sparse READ-ONLY git worktrees; each job owns private writable build/generated/trace/temp dirs; completed artifacts publish ATOMICALLY into a content-addressed cache keyed by (input hashes + flags + toolchain digest).
theory.prediction_a: 3 simultaneous real engine-build jobs (g++ compile of tools/constraint_ledger/trace_harness.cpp against the checked-out engine headers) complete with per-job source cost ~= working tree only -- the object store is paid ONCE; a per-lane full clone pays objects+tree per lane.
theory.prediction_b: A second wave of identical requests is a 100% cache hit (published artifact byte-identical to the fresh build, no recompile).
theory.prediction_c: All four falsifiers stay green under real concurrency.

F-CROSS-RUN-WRITE.fires_if: any job observed mutating ANOTHER job's outputs or the SHARED SOURCE, verified by (i) the construction guards (SourceView exposes no write API; view files OS-read-only 0o444; JobWorkspace.resolve refuses path escape; outputs sealed read-only on completion), (ii) an actual write attempt during the concurrent wave (must raise PermissionError/ValueError), (iii) post-wave re-hash of every view's tracked files vs pre-wave git blob ids and of every job's artifact vs its solo-run digest.
F-CROSS-RUN-WRITE.measurement: real concurrent builds: 3 simultaneous g++ jobs over their own sparse worktrees

F-CACHE-COLLISION.fires_if: any semantically different request (different input bytes, different flags, or different toolchain digest) resolves to a SHARED cache artifact -- i.e. two distinct canonical requests produce the same key, or a key lookup returns bytes matching the OTHER request's build.
F-CACHE-COLLISION.measurement: pairwise key distinctness across (-O0 vs -O2 flags), (original vs mutated input), (g++ vs different toolchain digest); artifact bytes must differ for distinct requests

F-PARTIAL-PUBLISH.fires_if: an interrupted publication is accepted by a reader: (i) a truncated envelope planted at the final cache name returns PARTIAL bytes or True on get(); (ii) an orphaned .tmp staging file is readable as an entry; (iii) a publisher killed mid-write leaves a readable entry; (iv) any digest mismatch in an envelope is returned to the caller instead of refused-and-rebuilt.
F-PARTIAL-PUBLISH.measurement: get() must return miss + record a refusal event for every partial form; atomic protocol = tmp staging dir (same volume) + fsync + re-read digest verify + os.replace

F-SOURCE-CLONE.fires_if: the tested workflow REQUIRES a per-lane duplicate source tree -- measured by byte census: bytes of (a) the shared object store, (b) one sparse read-only worktree view, (c) a real full clone; the 3-job workflow must complete with exactly ONE object store and per-job cost ~= view only, and build-dir reuse economics (wave-2 hits) reported.
F-SOURCE-CLONE.measurement: du census + git count-objects; duplication factor = per-lane clone cost / shared-store per-job cost

cache_key_schema.inputs: the REAL dependency closure from `g++ -MM` over the job's own view; private (generated) inputs hashed by content with a 'private:' prefix, repo files by repo-relative path
cache_key_schema.collision_resistance_note: distinct semantic requests -> distinct canonical JSON -> distinct keys; equality requires either identical semantics or a sha256 collision
